ict.name: Islamabad Capital Territory
ict.intro: Islamabad is the planned federal capital at the foot of the Margalla Hills. It is not a province, but it is treated here as its own unit so readers can open every sector, village and institution from one page.

districts.name: Islamabad
districts.about: Islamabad was designed in the 1960s as a planned garden capital at the foot of the Margalla Hills. The Faisal Mosque, Daman-e-Koh viewpoint, Saidpur Village and Bari Imam shrine sit alongside the government sector belt and a ring of fast-growing housing societies.
districts.education: Quaid-i-Azam University, NUST, COMSATS, IIUI and NUML anchor the city's large federal college and school network.
districts.health: The Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) and Polyclinic are the main public hospitals, backed by several private teaching hospitals.
districts.culture: People from every province live here, and hiking the Margalla trails or browsing the weekly bazaars are part of everyday life.
districts.issues: Traffic congestion, unplanned housing at the city's edges, and pressure on the Margalla Hills National Park are the main ongoing concerns.
districts.villages: Saidpur, Bari Imam, Shah Allah Ditta, Golra Sharif

districts.health: DHQ Attock and THQ hospitals in tehsils.
districts.culture: Potohari and Punjabi speech, river-side shrines and wheat-oilseed farms.
districts.issues: River erosion in places and the need to expand technical training.

faq_extra.q: When did Bajaur become a district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
faq_extra.a: Bajaur was a FATA tribal agency until the 25th Constitutional Amendment, signed on 31 May 2018, merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It is now a district of Malakand Division.

districts.name: Battagram
districts.about: Battagram sits on the Karakoram Highway in Hazara Division, with a cool hill climate around its market-town headquarters.
districts.education: The district runs government degree colleges; students looking for more specialised courses usually travel on to Mansehra or Abbottabad.
districts.health: DHQ Battagram is the main public hospital serving the tehsil.
districts.culture: Pashto and Hindko are both spoken across the surrounding hill villages.
districts.issues: Snowfall and monsoon landslides close stretches of the highway most years.
districts.villages: In January 2023, the neighbouring Allai tehsil was separated from Battagram and given full district status — it now has its own entry on this atlas.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Allai
districts.about: Allai is the mountain valley north of Battagram, historically ruled by its own Nawabs until 1971. It is a tehsil of Battagram District; district status has been announced but not yet notified.
districts.education: Education infrastructure is still catching up after the 2023 split; many students continue to travel to Battagram or Mansehra for higher study.
districts.health: A district headquarters hospital is being developed at Banna; patients previously relied on Battagram's DHQ.
districts.culture: The area was historically the princely state of Allai, ruled by its own Nawabs until 1971, and both Pashto and Hindko are spoken across its mountain villages.
districts.issues: Steep terrain and limited road access remain the main barrier to services reaching outlying villages.
districts.villages: Banna, Batila, Batkul, Biari, Jumbera, Pashto, Rushing and Shakargah union councils.
districts.status_note: Allai is a tehsil of Battagram District. A January 2023 notification giving it district status was not implemented; KP chief ministers announced district status again in May 2025 and February 2026, and in August 2026 it was still described as a tehsil to be upgraded. MyBook.Pk does not count it as a district until a notification is issued.

faq_extra.a: Two: Paharpur and Paniyala. The headquarters is Paharpur town.

districts.name: Hangu
districts.about: Hangu District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: 528,902 people in the 2023 census, 2 tehsils, headquarters Hangu.
districts.issues: A smaller tax base than neighbouring districts limits how much can be spent on public services.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Haripur
districts.about: Haripur is a Hazara district that combines farmland with industry at Hattar and proximity to Tarbela Dam.
districts.education: The University of Haripur and a number of colleges serve the district.
districts.health: DHQ Haripur is the main hospital.
districts.culture: Hindko-speaking towns are spread across the district.
districts.issues: Balancing industrial growth at Hattar with lake-shore planning around Tarbela is an ongoing concern.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Karak
districts.about: District south of Kohat that became separate on 1 July 1982; known for its rock salt, gypsum, oil and gas.
districts.issues: Despite the resource wealth, more colleges are still needed for women in the district.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

sources.title: About Karak

faq_extra.q: When did Karak become a district?
faq_extra.a: Karak became a separate district on 1 July 1982. Before that it was part of Kohat District.

districts.name: Khyber
districts.about: Khyber district takes its name from the historic Khyber Pass and was a tribal agency until the 2018 FATA merger.
districts.education: Colleges are expanding steadily as the district's education system is folded into the provincial one.
districts.culture: The Afridi tribe is dominant across the pass towns.
districts.issues: Merging former agency services fully into the provincial administrative system is an ongoing process.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Kohat
districts.about: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa district whose headquarters stands at the entrance to the Kohat Pass; Darra Adam Khel is one of its sub-divisions.
districts.issues: Balancing urban growth against the dry hills that surround the city is an ongoing planning challenge.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.issues: Road security and access to specialist medical care remain persistent challenges.

districts.name: Lakki Marwat
districts.about: Lakki Marwat covers the sandy southern plains of KP.
districts.education: The University of Lakki Marwat is the district's main higher-education institution.
districts.culture: The Marwat Pashtun tribe is dominant across the district's towns.
districts.issues: Dryland farming conditions and staffing the district's campuses are ongoing challenges.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Lower Dir
districts.about: Lower Dir covers the Panjkora valley below Upper Dir, with Timergara as its headquarters.
districts.education: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University in nearby Sheringal serves the wider Dir belt, alongside local colleges in Timergara.
districts.health: DHQ Timergara is the main hospital.
districts.culture: The population is a mix of Dir Kohistani and Pashtun communities.
districts.issues: River flooding is a recurring hazard in the valley.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Lower Kohistan
districts.about: District created on 15 January 2014 when Kohistan was divided; its headquarters is Pattan.
districts.issues: Landslides along the Karakoram Highway are a recurring problem.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

faq_extra.a: Notification No. 1075 of 15 January 2014 created Lower Kohistan out of Kohistan District, with Pattan as its headquarters.

districts.name: Malakand
districts.about: Malakand district sits at the historic Malakand Pass, the gateway between the Peshawar valley and Swat.
districts.education: The University of Malakand at nearby Chakdara and colleges in Batkhela serve the district.
districts.health: DHQ Batkhela is the main hospital.
districts.culture: The pass towns have long linked Peshawar-valley and Swat cultures.
districts.issues: Managing pass traffic alongside hill settlements is an ongoing concern.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Mansehra
districts.about: Hazara district whose headquarters lies on the Pakhli Plain; it includes the Kagan Valley and the Ashokan rock edicts near Mansehra town.
districts.issues: Tourism development along the road to Kaghan sometimes comes at the expense of investment in village schools.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Mardan
districts.about: Mardan is KP's second-largest city, built on the sugar and farm economy of the Yousafzai plain.
districts.education: Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan is the district's main institution of higher learning.
districts.health: Mardan Medical Complex is the district's principal hospital.
districts.culture: The plain towns include Takht-i-Bahi, a UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site.
districts.issues: Urban expansion is steadily encroaching on farmland around the city.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Mohmand
districts.about: Former FATA tribal agency, a district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Peshawar Division) since the 2018 merger.
districts.issues: Extending full provincial service delivery to the district remains an ongoing process after the FATA merger.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Nowshera
districts.about: Nowshera is a Kabul River and Grand Trunk Road district east of Peshawar, with cantonments at Nowshera, Risalpur and Cherat.

districts.health: Qazi Hussain Ahmad Medical Complex, Nowshera, is the district’s main medical teaching institute.
districts.culture: Pashto is the mother tongue of about 95% of residents; Hindko is the largest minority language (PBS 2023).
districts.issues: Kabul River flooding: the city of Nowshera was completely inundated in July 2010.
districts.villages: Nowshera Kalan, Jehangira, Pabbi, Amangarh and Akora Khattak are the census urban localities.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: North Waziristan
districts.about: Former FATA tribal agency, a district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Bannu Division) since the 2018 merger.
districts.issues: Rebuilding markets and schools after prolonged disruption remains a long-term task.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Orakzai
districts.about: Orakzai is a hill district in Kohat Division. It was Orakzai Agency from 1973 until the 2018 merger with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
districts.education: Literacy was 33.57% in 2023: 50.70% for men and 14.97% for women (PBS).
districts.health: Serious cases go to the district headquarters hospital at Kalaya, and many families travel to Kohat, Hangu or Peshawar (UN Women, 2020).
districts.culture: Pashto is the mother tongue of almost all residents (PBS 2023).
districts.issues: Mountain terrain limits access to services, and PBS 2023 counts the whole district as rural.
districts.villages: Kalaya, Samana, Feroz Khel, Zaira, Landok, Manawar and Khalwat.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Peshawar
districts.about: Peshawar is the provincial capital and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the region, blending the historic Qissa Khwani bazaar with new housing developments.
districts.education: The University of Peshawar, UET Peshawar, Khyber Medical University and Islamia College University together form one of the province's largest education clusters.
districts.health: Lady Reading Hospital, Hayatabad Medical Complex and Khyber Teaching Hospital are the city's major public hospitals.
districts.culture: Pashto literature and rubab music have deep roots here, centred on the city's historic caravan bazaar.
districts.issues: Air quality, traffic congestion and protecting the old city's built fabric are persistent challenges.
districts.villages: Badhber, Mathra and Regi rural areas.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Shangla
districts.about: Shangla District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: 891,252 people in the 2023 census, 5 tehsils, headquarters Alpuri.
districts.issues: Monsoon rains regularly cut roads in the district.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Swabi
districts.about: Swabi District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: 1,894,600 people in the 2023 census, 4 tehsils, headquarters Swabi.
districts.issues: Balancing industrial growth at Gadoon with the district's farmland is an ongoing concern.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Swat
districts.about: Former princely state on the Swat River; since January 2026 a district of four tehsils (Babuzai, Kabal, Charbagh and Barikot) with its headquarters at Gulkada.
districts.issues: Tourism crowding and recovery from the 2022 floods remain ongoing concerns.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit); Swat total is the sum of the 2023 rows of its 4 tehsils

districts.name: Bar Swat (Upper Swat)
districts.about: Bar Swat (Upper Swat) was notified as a separate district in January 2026, following a provincial cabinet decision of 19 December 2025. Its headquarters is Matta and it has three tehsils: Matta, Bahrain and Khwazakhela.
districts.education: Most higher education still runs through University of Swat's main campus in the remaining Swat district.
districts.health: New district health facilities are being organised in Matta; patients also use hospitals in Saidu Sharif.
districts.culture: The district covers the upper Swat valley including Kalam, Bahrain and Matiltan, long known as one of Pakistan's most scenic tourist areas.
districts.issues: Balancing tourism growth with village infrastructure is the main ongoing issue.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit); Bar Swat (Upper Swat) total is the sum of the 2023 rows of its 3 tehsils

districts.name: South Waziristan Upper
districts.about: South Waziristan Upper was created in April 2022, when the former South Waziristan district was divided in two, with Spinkai Raghazai as its headquarters.
districts.education: Colleges are being rebuilt and expanded across the district after years of conflict-related disruption.
districts.health: A district headquarters hospital serves Spinkai Raghazai and the surrounding tehsils.
districts.culture: The district is home to Mahsud tribes across valleys such as Ladha, Makin and Shawal.
districts.issues: Rebuilding markets, schools and roads after years of displacement remains an ongoing task.

districts.name: South Waziristan Lower
districts.about: South Waziristan Lower was created alongside South Waziristan Upper in April 2022, with Wana as its headquarters.
districts.education: Government colleges in and around Wana serve the district, with more courses added since the 2022 split.
districts.health: DHQ facilities in Wana handle most public healthcare needs.
districts.culture: The district is dominated by the Ahmadzai Wazir tribe, with Pashto spoken throughout.
districts.issues: Road security and rebuilding local markets remain priorities.
districts.villages: Wana, Shakai, Toi Khwla and Birmal.

districts.name: Tank
districts.about: Tank is a small southern district sitting at the edge of Waziristan.
districts.education: Government colleges serve the district's students.
districts.health: DHQ Tank is the main hospital.
districts.culture: The district shares the plains culture of southern KP.
districts.issues: Extreme summer heat and a small public-sector workforce limit service delivery.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Torghar
districts.about: Torghar is a small mountain district of Hazara Division, created out of Mansehra.
districts.education: College options are limited, and many students travel to Mansehra for further study.
districts.health: DHQ Torghar is the main hospital.
districts.culture: The district's Black Mountain villages give it its name (Torghar means "black mountain" in Pashto).
districts.issues: Extremely steep terrain makes road access difficult across much of the district.
districts.villages: Villages in the Judba side valleys.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Upper Dir
districts.about: Upper Dir covers the high country toward the Lowari Pass and the Kumrat valley.
districts.education: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University in Sheringal serves the district.
districts.health: DHQ Dir is the main hospital.
districts.culture: The Kumrat forests and Dir Kohistan region are central to the district's identity.
districts.issues: Tourism road development and forest protection sometimes pull in opposite directions.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Upper Kohistan
districts.about: Upper Kohistan covers the Indus gorge around the Dasu Dam project.
districts.education: Colleges in Dassu serve the district.
districts.health: DHQ Upper Kohistan is the main hospital.
districts.culture: Kohistani river villages line the gorge.
districts.issues: Dam-related resettlement and landslides on the Karakoram Highway are ongoing concerns.
districts.villages: Villages in the side valleys near Dassu.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

districts.name: Kolai-Palas
districts.about: Kolai-Palas is one of KP's newest districts, formed from the left bank of the Indus in the Kohistan region.
districts.education: A new college network is still being set up in the district.
districts.health: DHQ Kolai-Palas is the main hospital.
districts.culture: Kohistani villages make up the district's population.
districts.issues: Building new district offices and staff housing from scratch remains an early-stage task.
districts.population_source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 (area, population, density, urban proportion, household size and growth rate by administrative unit)

gb.name: Gilgit-Baltistan
gb.intro: Gilgit-Baltistan is the meeting of the Karakoram, Himalaya and Hindu Kush. Districts here are valleys more than plains. Read each one before you plan a school project or a journey.

districts.name: Astore
districts.about: High district toward Nanga Parbat’s Rupal side and Deosai approach.
districts.education: Colleges in Astore.

districts.name: Diamer
districts.about: Indus gorge at Chilas, under Nanga Parbat.
districts.education: Colleges in Chilas.
districts.issues: KKH slides and summer heat in the gorge.

districts.name: Ghanche
districts.about: Eastern Baltistan toward the Siachen approach valleys. Khaplu palace country.
districts.education: Colleges in Khaplu.

districts.name: Ghizer
districts.about: Western district toward Shandur and Yasin (Yasin / Gupis later split in some notifications).
districts.education: Colleges in Gahkuch.

districts.name: Gilgit
districts.about: Capital district at the meeting of rivers.
districts.education: Karakoram International University.
districts.culture: A bazaar of many mountain languages.
districts.issues: City growth on a narrow valley floor.

districts.name: Hunza
districts.about: High literacy, terraces and tourism under Rakaposhi and Ladyfinger.
districts.education: Colleges in Aliabad and Karimabad.
districts.culture: Burushaski and Wakhi, apricot and music.
districts.issues: Tourism load and Attabad-style lake risk.

districts.name: Kharmang
districts.about: Baltistan district on the Indus toward the Line of Control.
districts.education: Colleges in Tolti.

districts.name: Nagar
districts.about: Across the river from Hunza, under Hopper and Hispar glaciers.
districts.education: Colleges in Nagar.

districts.name: Shigar
districts.about: Valley of the Shigar River and the road toward Concordia / Baltoro.
districts.education: Colleges in Shigar.

districts.name: Skardu
districts.about: Main town of Baltistan on the Indus, gateway to Deosai and the high peaks.
districts.education: University of Baltistan and colleges.

districts.name: Roundu
districts.about: Created from Skardu belt on the Indus.
districts.education: Colleges being listed in local notices.

districts.name: Gupis-Yasin
districts.about: Split from Ghizer toward Shandur.
districts.education: Colleges in Yasin and Gupis.

districts.name: Darel
districts.about: Indus-right valley district created in the Diamer belt.
districts.education: Local colleges.

districts.name: Tangir
districts.about: Sister valley of Darel in the Diamer highlands.
districts.education: Local colleges.

district_count.basis: Gilgit-Baltistan government notification of June 2019 (four new districts, 14 in total).

sources.title: Four new districts set up in GB
sources.note: GB government notification of four new districts (Darel, Tangir, Roundu, Gupis-Yasin); 14 districts in total.

ajk.name: Azad Jammu and Kashmir
ajk.intro: Azad Jammu and Kashmir is administered through its own government, with ten districts in three divisions. Valleys of Neelum and Jhelum shape daily life.

districts.name: Muzaffarabad
districts.about: Capital at the meeting of Neelum and Jhelum. Rebuilt after the 2005 earthquake.
districts.education: University of AJK and colleges.

districts.name: Hattian Bala
districts.about: Jhelum valley district created after 2005.
districts.education: Colleges in Hattian.

districts.name: Neelum
districts.about: Long north-east valley along the Neelum River.
districts.education: Colleges in Athmuqam and Sharda.
districts.issues: Single-road access in winter and monsoon.

districts.name: Mirpur
districts.about: Mangla lake city with a large overseas Kashmiri link to Britain.
districts.education: MUST and colleges.
districts.villages: Dadyal (now often its own discussion), Islamgarh

districts.name: Bhimber
districts.about: Southern-most AJK district toward the Punjab plain.
districts.education: Colleges in Bhimber and Samahni.
districts.issues: Heat compared with the northern valleys.

districts.name: Kotli
districts.about: Central-south AJK on the Poonch river system.
districts.education: University of Kotli and colleges.

districts.name: Poonch (Rawalakot)
districts.about: Hill town of Rawalakot, often called the Pearl Valley.
districts.education: Poonch Medical College and public university presence.

districts.name: Bagh
districts.about: Hill district badly hit in 2005, since rebuilt as a district headquarters.
districts.education: Colleges in Bagh.

districts.name: Haveli
districts.about: Eastern district toward the Line of Control.
districts.education: Colleges in Forward Kahuta.

districts.name: Sudhanoti
districts.about: Hill district of Pallandri.
districts.education: Cadet College Palandri and public colleges.
districts.villages: Trarkhel, Baloch villages of the district
